candidates.title: button-behavior-and-examples
candidates.section: Buttons to handle expensive or file-writing processes
candidates.text: Astute observers may think, "This feels a little like caching." We are only saving results relative to one parameter, but the pattern could easily be expanded to save results relative to both parameters. In that sense, yes, it has some similarities to caching, but also some important differences. When you save results in `st.session_state`, the results are only available to the current user in their current session. If you use [`st.cache_data`](/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.cache_data) instead, the results are available to all users across all sessions. Furthermore, if you want to update a saved result, you have to clear all saved results for that function to do so.

candidates.title: st.multiselect without key drops the user's selection when options come in a different order on rerun
candidates.section: st.multiselect without key drops the user's selection when options come in a different order on rerun > Summary
candidates.text:
### Summary

If `st.multiselect` has no `key` and its `options` list comes back in a different order on the next run, every selection the user makes is thrown away. The widget briefly shows the new chip, then flickers back to the default. Passing `sorted(options)` makes it work, and so does setting any `key`.

The order of options is often unstable in real apps: `list(set(...))`, `df[col].unique()` after a filter, SQL queries without `ORDER BY`, dict/set unions, and "move selected to top" patterns.

Similar reports were closed as expected behavior (#5995, #8496). #11277 fixed the case where `key` is set. The keyless case still resets, even though multiselect doesn't need it to.

candidates.section: **Version 1.63.0**
candidates.text:
## **Version 1.63.0**

_Release date: September 1, 2026_

**Highlights**

- 🎯 Introducing event-scoped fragment reruns, which let a widget callback rerun just one named fragment:
    - Name a fragment with `@st.fragment(key=…)` and target it with [`st.rerun`](/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.rerun)`("filters")` or `st.rerun(["alpha", "beta"])` from an `on_change` or `on_click` callback ([#16161](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16161)).
    - `st.rerun()` and `st.switch_page()` now take effect inside widget callbacks instead of being discarded with a warning; apps that relied on the previous no-op will now rerun ([#16158](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16158)).
- ✨ Introducing `on_change="ignore"`, a new mode that updates a widget in the browser without rerunning your app. Your script receives the buffered value on the next rerun, such as a button click, and the mode is available on [`st.slider`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.slider) and [`st.text_input`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.text_input) ([#14828](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14828), [#16605](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16605)).
- 🍿 Introducing `type="step"` for [`st.expander`](/develop/api-reference/layout/st.expander) and [`st.status`](/develop/api-reference/status/st.status), which renders containers as a connected timeline — well suited to showing an agent's or a pipeline's progress ([#16558](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16558), [#13248](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13248)).

**Notable Changes**

candidates.title: widget-behavior
candidates.section: widget-behavior > Understanding widget behavior > Statefulness of widgets > Widgets do not persist when not continually rendered > Save widget values in Session State to preserve them between pages
candidates.text:
#### Save widget values in Session State to preserve them between pages

If you want to navigate away from a widget and return to it while keeping its value, use a separate key in `st.session_state` to save the information independently from the widget. This technique is also recommended to carry a widget's state to a new instance on another page. In this example, an underscore-prefixed, temporary key is used with a widget. Hence, `"_my_key"` is used as the widget key, but the data is copied to `"my_key"` to preserve it between pages.

```python
import streamlit as st

def store_value():
    # Copy the value to the permanent key
    st.session_state["my_key"] = st.session_state["_my_key"]

# Copy the saved value to the temporary key
st.session_state["_my_key"] = st.session_state["my_key"]
st.number_input("Number of filters", key="_my_key", on_change=store_value)
```

If this is functionalized to work with multiple widgets, it could look something like this:

```python
import streamlit as st

def store_value(key):
    st.session_state[key] = st.session_state["_"+key]
def load_value(key):
    st.session_state["_"+key] = st.session_state[key]

load_value("my_key")
st.number_input("Number of filters", key="_my_key", on_change=store_value, args=["my_key"])
```

candidates.title: Altair/Vega-Lite native toolbar: hover the download icon to choose PNG or SVG
candidates.section: Altair/Vega-Lite native toolbar: hover the download icon to choose PNG or SVG > Why?
candidates.text:
### Why?

I'm always frustrated when I hover an Altair/Vega-Lite chart, see the native download icon beside Fullscreen, click it, and can only get PNG.

For reports and papers I often need SVG (vector, scalable) as well as PNG. The old Vega-Embed ⋯ menu offered "Save as PNG" / "Save as SVG". After https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15806, that menu is gone, SVG export is gone, and `usermeta.embedOptions` can no longer restore export actions.

Workarounds (custom HTML components, extra `st.download_button`s, or DOM hacks) either leave the native toolbar unused or drift out of style as Streamlit's toolbar design changes. There is no public API to attach a format menu to the existing toolbar download button.

Related but different: #8177 is about PNG resolution, not choosing a format.

candidates.title: widget-behavior
candidates.section: Widgets do not persist when not continually rendered
candidates.text:
### Widgets do not persist when not continually rendered

If a widget command for a specific widget instance isn't called during a script run, then none of its parts are retained, including its value in `st.session_state`. If a widget has a key and you navigate away from that widget, its key and associated value in `st.session_state` are deleted. Even temporarily hiding a widget causes it to reset when it reappears; Streamlit will treat it like a new widget. To preserve widget state across pages or when widgets are temporarily hidden, save the value to a separate placeholder key as shown below.

candidates.text:
## Option 2: Save your widget values into a dummy key in Session State

If you want to navigate away from a widget and return to it while keeping its value, or if you want to use the same widget on multiple pages, use a separate key in `st.session_state` to save the value independently from the widget. In this example, a temporary key is used with a widget. The temporary key uses an underscore prefix. Hence, `"_my_key"` is used as the widget key, but the data is copied to `"my_key"` to preserve it between pages.

```python
import streamlit as st

def store_value():
    # Copy the value to the permanent key
    st.session_state["my_key"] = st.session_state["_my_key"]

# Copy the saved value to the temporary key
st.session_state["_my_key"] = st.session_state["my_key"]
st.number_input("Number of filters", key="_my_key", on_change=store_value)
```

If this is functionalized to work with multiple widgets, it could look something like this:

```python
import streamlit as st

def store_value(key):
    st.session_state[key] = st.session_state["_"+key]
def load_value(key):
    st.session_state["_"+key] = st.session_state[key]

load_value("my_key")
st.number_input("Number of filters", key="_my_key", on_change=store_value, args=["my_key"])
```

candidates.section: container.empty() not explicitly clearing when refreshes/streaming data is needed via st.rerun() > Related Issues
candidates.text:
### Related Issues

- **#12069** — [st.empty does not clear removed elements](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12069): Very likely a duplicate. Reports the same core behavior where `st.empty()` containers fail to clear old elements if new content has fewer items, leaving ghost elements visible. Confirmed bug, P3.
- **#10126** — [`st.close()` or `st.end()` to remove stale elements mid-run](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10126): A feature request that directly addresses the underlying limitation. Proposes a mechanism to explicitly discard remaining stale elements within a container before the script run finishes, which would solve this issue.
- **#5044** — [empty() does not remove cleared elements?](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5044): A long-standing related bug where `.empty()` clears the UI but doesn't fully remove internal widget state, leading to DuplicateWidgetID errors. Confirmed bug, P3.

candidates.section: Define your user authentication pages
candidates.text:
1. Begin your logout page (function definition).

   ```python
   def logout():
   ```

1. Immediately set the role to `None` and rerun the app.

   ```python
       st.session_state.role = None
       st.rerun()
   ```

   Since the lougout page function immediately updates Session State and reruns, a user will never view this page. The page will execute in a fraction of a second and, upon rerunning, the app will send the user to the login page. Therefore, no additional elements are rendered on the page. If desired, you can change this page to also include a button, similar to the login page. A button would allow users to confirm they really intend to log out.

candidates.title: st.tabs collapses into a stacked column after certain session-state interactions on 1.59.0 (works on 1.58.x)
candidates.section: Summary
candidates.text:
### Summary

st.tabs([...]) renders correctly on the first page load, but after a chain of nested widget interactions (in our case: submit a form → click a computation button → select a CSV from the training-library st.selectbox inside a nested expander) the tab widget flattens on the next rerun: all with tab_X: block contents render as a single scrollable column with no tab bar. Downgrading to streamlit<1.59 (latest 1.58.x) restores the tab widget with no other code changes.

Broken: streamlit==1.59.0 (released 2026-07-06).
Working: streamlit<1.59 (latest 1.58.x).

Source
https://github.com/Fodera-Laboratory/PEARL-app — pinned to streamlit<1.59 in requirements.txt for the moment.

candidates.title: button-behavior-and-examples
candidates.section: button-behavior-and-examples > Button behavior and examples > Summary
candidates.text:
## Summary

Buttons created with [`st.button`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.button) do not retain state. They return `True` on the script rerun resulting from their click and immediately return to `False` on the next script rerun. If a displayed element is nested inside `if st.button('Click me'):`, the element will be visible when the button is clicked and disappear as soon as the user takes their next action. This is because the script reruns and the button return value becomes `False`.

In this guide, we will illustrate the use of buttons and explain common misconceptions. Read on to see a variety of examples that expand on `st.button` using [`st.session_state`](/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.session_state). [Anti-patterns](#anti-patterns) are included at the end. Go ahead and pull up your favorite code editor so you can `streamlit run` the examples as you read. Check out Streamlit's [Basic concepts](/get-started/fundamentals/main-concepts) if you haven't run your own Streamlit scripts yet.

candidates.title: button-behavior-and-examples
candidates.section: A slight problem
candidates.text:
#### A slight problem

In this example, we access `st.session_state.name` both before and after the buttons which modify it. When a button ("**Jane**" or "**John**") is clicked, the script reruns. The info displayed before the buttons lags behind the info written after the button. The data in `st.session_state` before the button is not updated. When the script executes the button function, that is when the conditional code to update `st.session_state` creates the change. Thus, this change is reflected after the button.

```python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

if 'name' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state['name'] = 'John Doe'

st.header(st.session_state['name'])

if st.button('Jane'):
    st.session_state['name'] = 'Jane Doe'

if st.button('John'):
    st.session_state['name'] = 'John Doe'

st.header(st.session_state['name'])
```

candidates.title: container.empty() not explicitly clearing when refreshes/streaming data is needed via st.rerun()
candidates.section: Additional Information
candidates.text:
### Additional Information

_No response_

This issue reports that calling `container.empty()` followed by `st.rerun()` does not immediately clear the container's contents on the frontend. Instead, the old elements linger as "stale" (greyed-out) elements until the next script run fully completes. The root cause is in how Streamlit's render tree works: when a new script run begins, keyed containers inherit their children from the previous run (see `addBlock` in `AppRoot.ts`). These inherited children are marked as stale (via `isElementStale` in `Block/utils.ts`) and rendered with reduced opacity, but they are only actually removed from the tree when `clearStaleNodes` is called at the **end** of the script run. In the reporter's case, a `time.sleep(2)` polling loop means stale elements remain visible for the full duration of each run, causing a "pulsing" effect. The `container.empty()` call from the previous run has no lasting effect since the container is re-created with inherited children in the new run.

candidates.section: Additional Information

### Additional Information

_No response_

Hey [USER] Thank you for the issue! I believe this is an expected behavior. Widgets that don't appear in the run are deleted. Here's what's happening:

1. Text is updated in string
2. Button is pressed and rerun occurs (but the the text was never rendered. Widget is reset
3. Widget reverts back to default

If you move the rerun button _after_ the text input. Everything works as expected. If you want it before the text input, you can leverage `st.empty()` like in this example:

```python
import streamlit as st

@st.fragment()
def toggle_and_text():
    foo = st.empty()
    t = st.text_input("Enter t:",value='foo', key='t')
    st.info(f't = {t}')
    if foo.button("rerun"):
        st.rerun()

toggle_and_text()
st.header('Outside Fragment')
st.info(f'session_state_t = {st.session_state.t}')
st.button("Update")
```

I'll probably close this issue, but feel free to ask any questions
